title: Brownfield specification mining
summary: Recover the observable behavior, invariants and test anchors of legacy code so a change can be specified against what the system actually does, not what its comments claim.

provenance.notes: Restated as a read-only workflow whose output is a list of testable statements, each tied to code or an existing test.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The module, function or endpoint whose behavior must be specified.

inputs.name: change
inputs.description: The intended change, if known, so the spec can focus on the affected surface.

outputs.name: behavior-list
outputs.description: Numbered observable behaviors, each with the file and test that evidence it.

outputs.name: gaps
outputs.description: Behaviors with no test and no clear code evidence, ranked by risk for the intended change.

workflow.step: Identify the public surface of the target: exported symbols, routes, CLI flags, persisted formats and error values.
workflow.check: The surface is enumerated from code, not from documentation.

workflow.step: For each surface element, read the implementation and write one sentence of observable behavior in input-to-output terms, including error and boundary cases.
workflow.check: Each sentence can be falsified by a test.

workflow.step: Find existing tests and map them to the sentences; mark every sentence with no covering test as unpinned.
workflow.check: Mapping cites test function names you opened.

workflow.step: Flag behaviors that look accidental (undocumented defaults, ordering dependence, swallowed errors) and say whether the intended change may legitimately alter them.
workflow.check: Accidental behavior is labelled as such, not silently preserved or dropped.

workflow.step: Recommend characterization tests for unpinned behaviors on the change path, before any implementation starts.

constraints: Read-only: describe behavior, never modify the code or run it.
Do not turn a comment or docstring into a behavior without matching code.
Keep the mined specification separate from the proposed new behavior.

examples.title: Pagination edge
examples.situation: A legacy list endpoint is being changed; no spec exists.
examples.guidance: Record what it returns for page zero, an out-of-range page and an empty set, cite the test or note the gap, and recommend characterization tests for the gaps.

verification: Every behavior statement cites code or a test.
Unpinned behaviors on the change path are listed with a recommended test.

task.text: Reverse engineer the undocumented behavior of the legacy export function before the rewrite.
We need characterization tests and an invariant list for the existing behavior of the parser.
Reverse engineer why the legacy loop panics.
Plan the new endpoint from scratch with a clean schema.
